security_spec.violation_condition: When executing vsetvli/vsetvl with rs1==x0 and rd==x0, QEMU writes the new vtype unconditionally (vector_helper.c:125) without first saving and comparing the old LMUL/SEW ratio against the new one. If the LMUL/SEW ratio changes but the old vl happens to still fit within the new VLMAX (e.g., old vl=4, ratio change keeps vlmax large enough), QEMU does NOT set vill=1 and does NOT zero vl, because the only guard (rvv_vsetvl_x0_vill knob, default off, line 119) checks 'env->vl != vl' rather than checking 'old_ratio != new_ratio'.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: helper_vsetvl writes env->vtype without saving old LMUL/SEW; ratio-change check missing or confused with vl-change check; rvv_vsetvl_x0_vill knob gating fraction of the required behavior
security_spec.summary: QEMU helper_vsetvl lacks the mandatory LMUL/SEW ratio-change check for the rs1==x0,rd==x0 keep-vl case; it gates incomplete behavior behind a non-default knob that tests vl-change instead of ratio-change, so a ratio change with coincidentally-valid old vl proceeds without vill=1, leaving guest with inconsistent {vtype,vl} state.

findings.finding: rvv_vsetvl_x0_vill knob defaults to false (cpu.c:2696), so by default QEMU never sets vill for vsetvl/vsetvli with rs1=x0 && rd=x0 even when the new SEW/LMUL ratio would change VLMAX. The spec (vector-common.adoc:1298) requires this form 'can only be used when VLMAX and hence vl is not actually changed by the new SEW/LMUL ratio' — use with a changing ratio is reserved and implementations may set vill. QEMU silently accepts the illegal usage by default, writing the new vtype unconditionally (line 125) without checking old vs new VLMAX.

No check for pre-existing env->vill == 1 before computing vl/vtype for the rs1=x0 && rd=x0 case. The spec (vector-common.adoc:1298) states: 'Use of the instructions is also reserved if vill was 1 beforehand. Implementations may set vill in either case.' QEMU only checks the vill bit from the NEW vtype value s2 (line 72), never reads env->vill. A guest that calls vsetvl with rs1=x0,rd=x0 while vill=1 should have the instruction treated as reserved, but QEMU proceeds to compute new vl/vtype without detecting the pre-existing vill condition.

Even with rvv_vsetvl_x0_vill=true, the check uses 'env->vl != vl' to detect ratio changes, rather than comparing old VLMAX against new VLMAX. This can miss cases where the SEW/LMUL ratio changes (and thus VLMAX changes) but the old vl happens to still fit within the new VLMAX, e.g. old VLMAX=1, vl=1, new VLMAX=2 gives vl=min(1,2)=1 so env->vl==vl passes but VLMAX changed. The spec's NOTE (vector-common.adoc:1300-1308) primarily concerns VLMAX shrinking, but the normative text says 'VLMAX... is not actually changed' without qualification.
